correctness.rationale: Rechecked the complete repaired claim. First-jet evaluation at a rational point has a three-dimensional target; a kernel member has zero value and both derivatives, so dimension four is impossible. The last three coefficient positions of the corrected generators are the identity. A fresh exact recomputation on the 13 projective triples gave 52 unit affine Jacobian ideals over F3 and separately verified all binary discriminants squarefree including infinity. Field extension preserves the unit ideals. For a three-dimensional all-smooth space, a rational base point would reduce the first-jet image to dimension at most two, again a contradiction. This proves only the corrected base-point conclusion. For the original inclusion-maximal reading, tuples (0,0,1,1,0,0,0,0,1) and (0,1,0,0,0,1,1,0,1) in the frozen monomial order span an all-smooth pencil vanishing at ([1:0],[1:0]). Enumerating all 3^9 coefficient vectors gives 10,360 smooth candidate vectors outside the pencil and none for which all nine translates by the pencil are smooth. In odd characteristic the squarefree discriminant criterion is also necessary here: a fiber component would meet the positive-degree residual restriction or be nonreduced; otherwise the quadratic local form near a branch value is y^2=g(x), singular for a multiple root. The corrected RESULT.md does not claim a census or smoothness of arbitrary geometric linear combinations.

value.rationale: The natural anticanonical linear-system problem asks whether the universal first-jet obstruction is sharp over a small field, where random smooth members do not make every rational linear combination smooth. Producing a dimension-attaining geometric genus-one net, rather than isolated smooth sections or pencils, answers this exact question. The corrected base-point statement describes a necessary feature of such extremizers.
